author: ShiptheBattle
body:
Avicore has two new games, a lot more kits, a lot more maps, a lot more people and a lot more changes. Obvious, right? 

Well, most of these are some fairly nice additives, but when it comes to the two last ones I mentioned, I'm not sure most people would agree these are nice. 
Of course funky loves more people, because that means more popularity, which means more money. 
But, to us users, this popularity rise may not be as good. There's so much more hackers, the games are decked up full for some games and so much more... different people, as in rude people. I can't, (Not exaggerating) CAN'T go to one game of Nebula with 30+ people without having a guy block my monument, without a guy having to spam the chat, without a guy being downright rude and annoying or without a guy hacking his head off. 

It's sort of depressing when the old Avicus had, to me, 1 hacker every 30 so games, and 1 rude person every 3-5 games or so. Although we have 5x'ed our old population, there comes many many bad features to it. And it does also really piss me off when it's extraordinarily hard to get a mod here and then being too lazy to actually screenshot and then report on the forums. The most a regular person would do is report, and it turns out, usually nothing really happens, sadly.

Furthermore, due to the recent changes, many more types of hacks are allowed, there's many reporting bugs and just gives mod a harder time.

Back to the point about the population increase, because there are SO many more people on Avicus, I do believe that we need more and more moderators. With only approximately 4 dozen staff that are able to help, they seriously can't fight the force of several hundreds of rude people and hackers.

To clarify, I seriously don't want people to think that this post is for my sake only, to increase my chances of becoming a mod higher and for my "Reviewing" to be accepted, but seriously, to actually get this out to people on the server and ask what they think about the server.

replies.author: hercules_the_dog
replies.body:
If you increase the population of a server, there's still going to be the same percentage of hackers/rule breakers/jerks etc. You wouldn't really be noticing more of them unless you had a server the size of less than 100 people or something to begin with. So it's not about experiencing more hackers (this is assuming you play the same amount of games as before the server increased in amount of people), but needing more moderators to deal with more hackers, which is something that the typical player doesn't need to worry about. The player experience is worsened in no way by the onset of an increase in players. In rare cases, when the population bump is large-scaled, there might be a drop in average knowledge of the game, but really it's not going to lead to the effects you list here.
As for decrease in quality/amount of moderator responses to reports, it's something that you really don't need to worry about dealing with. It's completely up to the staff, and they'd certainly know if there were too many reports to respond to.
The only thing necessary that is listed here is an increase in moderators, which should be proportional to the population of the server. The amount of moderators is entirely up to the staff, and as I said earlier, they would know if they had a problem.

replies.author: goldenwalrus909
replies.body:
Think of it like this:
Say 10% of everyone is a hacker.
If we currently have 500 players on, we'll have 50 hackers.
If we have 1000 players on, we'll have 100 hackers.
If we have 250 players on, 25 will be hackers.
Since the hackers are a fraction of the players, you have to multiply both the numerator (Hackers) and the denominator (Players) by the same number to make it proportional. 
300/30= 900/90
